thread:
maria_sales: FYI — new POC kickoff with FinBank next week. They want a private deployment in their AWS account. Main asks: should we do VPC peering or PrivateLink? firewall egress only 443? need static IPs for allowlist, and SOC needs a network diagram + short blurb for their security questionnaire. Also pricing question: if they exceed free credits, how does Dedicated pricing for POC look? can someone own the tech convo?

ashley_se: I can own the tech side. High level: PrivateLink is usually the path of least resistance for locked-down AWS orgs (no route table changes, endpoint sits in their subnet via ENIs + NLB on our side). Peering works too but requires route updates and care with overlapping CIDRs.

kevin_net: Quick network notes:
- PrivateLink: customer creates interface endpoint (ENIs) in a subnet, traffic goes to our NLB -> target. Allowlist is by IP ranges for the NLB or by AWS-managed prefix list we can provide.
- VPC peering: L3, direct route, needs security group / NACL adjustments on both sides; no transitive routing.
- For egress: we only require outbound HTTPS (443) to our endpoints for API traffic. No UDP ports needed for inference/metrics.

ashley_se: Example minimal SG outbound we recommend for PrivateLink case:
```
# customer SG outbound
Type: HTTPS  Protocol: TCP  Port: 443  Destination: <redwood-nlb-cidr-or-prefix-list>
# if they use NAT/proxy, allow our endpoints over 443 as well
```
Also enable Private DNS for the interface endpoint so existing hostnames resolve to the VPC endpoint.

maria_sales: they specifically asked for static IPs to put in a corporate firewall allowlist. can we provide static IPs?

kevin_net: We can provide a small list of stable NLB IPs per region for the POC (not a global single IP). For production, we recommend using the published prefix lists or the PrivateLink interface (endpoint) which is inside their VPC so no outbound allowlist needed. If they insist on peering we can give the peered subnet CIDRs that our deployment will live in.

sam_eng: Pricing/POC note: we can offer a time-limited Dedicated trial or reserved sandbox w/ a small commit. For sales details i can follow up with an estimate. For POC sizing tell me expected requests/sec and avg tokens so I can suggest Dedicated vs hosted with burst.

sec_bot: Security checklist items from SOC: TLS 1.2+ required, certs managed by us for hosted endpoints. For Private deployments we support customer-provided certs and KMS/HSM integrations. They may ask for audit logs — we can provide request logs and CloudTrail integration for Private. mTLS is available for PrivateLink if they want mutual auth.

ashley_se: Additional gotchas:
- DNS: if they use split-horizon DNS, enable PrivateLink private DNS.
- Egress NAT: if they go through corporate proxy, we can support it but need proxy allowlist for hostname + cert pinning details.
- CIDR overlap: peering fails on overlap — ask them to confirm VPC CIDRs early.

maria_sales: perfect. Can you also produce a simple network diagram + one-pager for their security questionnaire? target delivery = EOD tomorrow if possible. POC start target = Tue next week.

ashley_se: will do. I'll attach a one-pager + PNG diagram and a bullet list of the firewall rules and prefix lists. I'll also provide a temporary set of NLB IPs for the POC. :thumbsup:

kevin_net: I'll validate the SG/NACL text and confirm the CIDR we plan to use for the peered subnet (if they pick peering).

sam_eng: I'll prepare a POC pricing note and options (hosted w/ credits, small Dedicated commit, or Private with support add-on). Will follow up in a separate thread with numbers.

maria_sales: awesome — owners: ashley = tech + docs/diagram, kevin = network rules validation, sam = pricing/commit. I'll schedule kickoff and loop in their cloud infra lead. thanks everyone!

ashley_se: noted — sending docs offline shortly.

sec_bot: Reminder: log all data access requests in the SOC ticketing system and attach the network diagram for review.
